scope: F07 decoy isolation: the C12 decoy handler runs inside a rootless container that has no network at all, no capabilities, no host namespace and a read-only root filesystem, bounded by a hard process and memory limit. The supervisor states the policy, the limited container provider applies it and the supervisor verifies the observed and the effective controls before it reports a running decoy. The engine starts the isolated decoy with --decoy-isolation and propagates the typed outcome.
source_identity_algorithm: SHA-256 of sorted UTF-8 relative path + NUL + raw SHA-256(file bytes) over tracked and non-ignored untracked files; docs/evidence/, plans/progress.json, docs/agents/SESSION_HANDOFF.json and SHA256SUMS.txt excluded because they publish this identity themselves.

limitations: No decoy surface is published: the container has no network at all, so the decoy address is reachable only from inside its own namespace. Publishing the decoy to untrusted peers with the outbound denial kept is later workflow work.
The engine workflow verifies one isolated decoy and removes it again; it does not keep a decoy running. A persistent decoy service is later workflow work.
The memory limit needs a rootless runtime with cgroup delegation. A runtime without it fails the policy verification; the limit is never reported as held because it was requested.
The provider is the only place that runs another program. It runs the container runtime with a fixed argument vector, without a shell and without a network client, and it never pulls an image.

The pinned image is not redistributed by MirageMesh. Its digest, platform, provenance and the license of every component are recorded in docs/engineering/toolchain-lock.json; the image contains a GPL-2.0-only busybox component, which the operator accepts by pulling it.

The decoy host of the tests is a test fixture, not a product listener: it exists so that the real C12 handler runs under the isolation policy and so that the probes measure the isolation from inside the container. The decoy artifact of the engine workflow is supplied by the operator; the decoy service binary is later work.

The state directory of the workflow must be writable by the operator: a rootless installation cannot write into /var/lib, so the examples use a user owned path and the engine refuses a state path that is not a private directory of the owner.
The C12 card and plans/roadmap.json are unchanged. The C12 evidence stays bound to its own historical source; the C12 anchor of the decoy package is extended, not weakened.
The original C13 delivery had no commit. A separate follow-up fix commit is authorized and created locally; no push or publication was performed.

The GitHub Actions runs for base commit 2e78097 failed while observing effective cgroup limits. The local fix reads those files through /proc/<container-pid>/root/sys/fs/cgroup instead of mapping Podman inspect CgroupPath into the runner mount, and passes the full race suite and clean-clone workflow locally. GitHub Actions on the updated source remain unverified; no commit or push was made.
